stage_a.note: Strong positive expression characterizes most of the presentation; he loves wine.
Sustained engagement with the subject is evident as he demonstrates the product.
Friendly, approachable and considerate expression characterizes much of the presentation.

venture.description: Premium wine packaged in single-serve, sealed plastic glasses for easy consumption outdoors and at events.
venture.note: The product focuses on convenience for outdoor events and stadiums.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 presents Copa Di Vino, single-serve premium wine in a glass, seeking 600k for 20 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if he is selling a packaging system or entering the competitive wine business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that he has a winery.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to clarify if he has a winery.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms he has a winery, makes 2500 cases a year, and is currently in market.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if he grows his own Chardonnay and Cabernet grapes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that he buys fruit from friends who have vineyards.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 hands out samples of Copa Di Vino to the panel and toasts.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokingly asks if that was the easiest glass of wine they ever served themselves.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 remarks that the seal is a little hard to take off.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees with S3's remark about the seal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if he is buying a wine label or a packaging system.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they have three revenue streams: licensing, bottling for industry, and their own brand.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks which of the three streams are bringing in sales today.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that their own consumer brand is bringing in sales right now.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what the current sales are for the consumer brand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers they have half a million in sales and 800k in orders over five months.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses positive surprise at the quick sales growth.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if people buy the product because it is easy to carry.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they buy it for convenience and because it is a good glass of wine.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 argues it is not premium wine but industrial wine.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 calls S2 a wine snob in defense of the product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 states he personally would not buy the wine.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 notes the mass market appeal and thinks the packaging is the real play.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how long the wine stays fresh in the packaging.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers it stays fresh for a year, overcoming the typical short shelf life.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if the packaging is patented.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms it is patented, explaining the technology prevents the seal from blowing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks who they are currently selling the product to.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers they are in discussions with Kroger, Ralphs, and 7-Eleven.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks why they are in the wine business instead of licensing to major wineries.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers they are working on projects with two of the largest wine companies.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how much money they estimate making from those deals.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 estimates three to five million dollars in sales next year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks why they are in the packaging business instead of marketing the patent to packaging companies.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the wine industry needs niche service companies and proof of concept first.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 agrees that the industry wants to see a proof of concept because they have seen failures.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 says pioneers get slaughtered, feels it is too early, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if there is a way to take the patent out of Copa Di Vino.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees he likes the patent and asks to pull the two apart.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 clarifies if they can separate the IP and leave F1 with the wine business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms they can separate the IP.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 suggests F1 come back to him with a valuation for the IP, cash, and stock.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 playfully notes that attendance at S5's stadiums is rising.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 acknowledges he could resell the product in his stadiums.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokes that he could still fill S5's cups.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 clarifies he does not want to be in the commission sales business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks how much of the IP and bottler company he could own for his 600k check.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers he would offer 20 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 states that 20 percent is not enough.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues that S2 has already devalued the brand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 defends the panel, saying they did not devalue it but just do not want that business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 says he will not try to split the business, does not want to build a brand, and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 says she cannot bring anything to the table and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 reiterates the real value is the IP and asks how much of that he can buy for 600k.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers he is not ready to give away his competitive advantages to another entity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 argues F1 is losing a huge opportunity, claiming the IP side makes less money.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 offers 600k for 51 percent of the IP, leaving F1 to run the brand and bottling.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues the opportunity is far greater than S2's offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 says S2's deal is better than what he would offer, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to explain his position clearer to the remaining investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 advises F1 to stop selling.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues he has invested heavily, built a successful business, and will not give away his special sauce.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if S2 will get an answer from F1.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 formally rejects S2's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 invites F1 to make a counteroffer for 51 percent of the IP.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters with three million dollars for the 51 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 immediately rejects the counteroffer and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 dramatically states he will drink a thousand dollar wine to weep for F1's lost opportunity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 tells F1 he looked a gift horse in the mouth.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees with S5's assessment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confidently toasts the panel and drinks his wine.

decisions.note: Pioneers get slaughtered, too early for him.
Does not want to split the business or build a wine brand.
Cannot bring anything to the table.

decisions.terms: $600k for 51% of the IP only, F1 keeps 49% and runs brand/bottling.
decisions.note: Believes the real money is in licensing the IP.
Would not offer a deal as good as S2's offer, does not want to be in the business.
Not willing to give away his special sauce.
Rejects the counteroffer as too high.
